instructions: Heat the broiler to high with a rack about 4 inches from the heat.
Cut the baguette into 4 pieces about 5 inches long and split each piece lengthwise. Lay the 8 pieces cut side up on a baking sheet and brush them with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Broil for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges are golden. Stay close, since the broiler goes from golden to burnt fast.
While the bread toasts, strip the leaves from 8 sprigs of thyme.
Crumble the goat cheese over the hot toast and press it flat with the back of a fork.
Sprinkle on the thyme and a few grinds of pepper, then drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the 3 tbsp honey.
method_notes: Cooking My Dreams (the lead) brushes sliced baguette with olive oil, toasts it, spreads it with softened goat cheese and finishes with honey and thyme. Steven Raichlen's Barbecue Bible tartines grill the bread and shingle slices of a goat cheese log with thyme, pepper, olive oil and honey, which is where the log and the serving size come from. Williams-Sonoma and most other versions add walnuts or pecans, which are left out here to keep it nut-free. Neither source has 20 ratings (the lead has 1), so this is a fallback lead.
